 Japan vs Brazil Today: Kubo and Nakamura Give Japan the Lead, Vinicius Junior Responds in Singapore
 Japan vs Brazil in Singapore sees Japan leading 2-1 thanks to goals from Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura, with Vinicius Junior pulling one back.
 By: Damar Prasetya 
 | 
 Editor: Nayla Savitri 
 | 
 Contributor: Niken Pramudya 
 November 14, 2026, 19:14 WITA · 6 min read 
 Brazil national team players duel with Japan players during the 2026 World Cup match in Houston, United States, June 29, 2026. (Photo: Archive) 
 SINGAPORE, Aktualita.co -  The Japan vs Brazil match is being fiercely contested in an international friendly at the Singapore National Stadium on Saturday (11/14/2026). Japan immediately applied pressure on the Samba team and managed to score two goals early on through Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura. 
 Brazil, appearing with a number of young players under the guidance of Carlo Ancelotti, did not remain silent. Vinicius Junior narrowed the deficit and revived his team's chances in the match, which is part of the November 2026 FIFA Matchday agenda.

 Based on live score updates around the 39th minute, Japan is temporarily leading 2-1. Kubo scored in the 15th minute, followed by Nakamura in the 19th minute, before Vinicius Junior replied in the 33rd minute. 
 This score is still temporary and not the final result of the match. 
 This meeting has garnered attention as it is the third duel between Japan and Brazil in approximately 13 months. The two countries previously defeated each other in a friendly match in October 2025 and the round of 32 of the 2026 World Cup. 
 For Japan, this match is an opportunity to show the development of their game after being eliminated from the World Cup. Meanwhile, Brazil is using it to test the consistency and depth of their squad ahead of the next international agenda. 
 Flow of the Japan vs Brazil Match, Japan Appears Aggressive 
 Japan entered the match with a fairly bold approach. Hajime Moriyasu's team tried to build attacks through quick movements between lines and by utilizing space behind the Brazilian defense. 
 The strategy resulted in the opening goal through Takefusa Kubo in the 15th minute. 
 The Real Sociedad player has become one of Japan's attacking engines with his ability to control the ball in tight spaces and connect the midfield play with the forwards. 
 Not long after the first goal, Japan again surprised the Brazilian defense. 
 Keito Nakamura doubled the Samurai Blue's lead in the 19th minute. Two goals in quick succession forced Brazil to chase the deficit early. 
 The situation demonstrated Japan's ability to capitalize on the momentum of the match. Neat organizational play and speed in transitioning from defense to attack have become important weapons against a team with high individual quality. 
 Brazil then responded through Vinicius Junior. 
 The Real Madrid forward scored in the 33rd minute, narrowing the gap to 2-1. The goal became an important momentum for Brazil to increase the pressure again. 
 Although it is a friendly match, both teams are showing quite tight competition. Japan is trying to maintain its lead, while Brazil is looking for gaps to equalize. 
 Japan vs Brazil Lineups November 14, 2026 
 Japan coach Hajime Moriyasu fielded a number of players who have been important parts of the national team in recent years. 
 Japan lineup: 
 Zion Suzuki; Shuto Nakano, Ayumu Seko, Koki Machida, Hiroki Ito; Ao Tanaka, Daichi Kamada; Ritsu Doan, Takefusa Kubo, Keito Nakamura; Daizen Maeda. 
 Meanwhile, Carlo Ancelotti gave opportunities to a combination of young and experienced players. 
 Brazil lineup: 
 Pedro Morisco; Wesley, Jair Cunha, Gabriel Magalhaes, Carlos Augusto; Andrey Santos, Bruno Guimaraes, Andre Luiz; Estevao, Raphinha, Vinicius Junior. 
 This composition shows that Brazil is still in the process of forming a team framework after the 2026 World Cup. 
 The decision to place young players in several sectors is part of an effort to expand tactical options. Brazil does not only need players with individual ability, but also balance when facing opponents with strong organizational play like Japan. 
 Carlo Ancelotti Still Testing Brazil's Strength 
 The match against Japan is one of the important tests for Carlo Ancelotti in building a new generation of the Brazilian national team. 
 Before the match, the Italian coach emphasized that the series of friendly matches in Singapore is part of the team development process to face the challenges of the coming years. 
 "The goal is to develop in a balanced way and prepare a group of players to face the challenges that lie ahead." 
 — Carlo Ancelotti, in an official statement ahead of the friendly match series in Singapore, translated from English. 
 Ancelotti is not just prioritizing the match result. He also wants to know how the players adapt to the game system and face pressure from quality opponents. 
 Japan is a suitable opponent to test those aspects. 
 The East Asian team is known for having discipline in defense, dynamic player movement, and the ability to counterattack quickly. 
 These characteristics require Brazilian players to maintain coordination both when in possession of the ball and when losing possession. 
 Japan vs Brazil Head-to-Head Record, Samba Team Still Leads 
 Historically, Brazil still has a much better record than Japan. 
 Before the November 14, 2026 match, the two countries had met 15 times at the senior men's national team level. 
 Of that number, Brazil recorded 12 wins, Japan one win, and two matches ended in a draw. 
 Brazil also leads in goal productivity with 39 goals, while Japan has scored nine goals. 
 However, the last two meetings show that the competition is no longer one-sided. 
 On October 14, 2025, Japan recorded a historic 3-2 victory over Brazil in a friendly match in Tokyo. 
 That result was Japan's first victory in the history of meetings with the Samba team. 
 Brazil then avenged that defeat on June 29, 2026, when the two countries met in the round of 32 of the World Cup. 
 In the match that took place in Houston, United States, Japan took the lead first through Kaishu Sano. 
 Brazil managed to bounce back through a Casemiro goal before Gabriel Martinelli secured a 2-1 victory in extra time. 
 The result ended Japan's journey in the tournament and sent Brazil to the round of 16. 
 Therefore, the meeting in Singapore has its own value for both teams, even though they are not competing for tickets or official competition trophies. 
 Next Schedule for Japan and Brazil 
 After the match on Saturday, both countries still have international agendas in Singapore. 
 Japan is scheduled to face Paraguay on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. The match will be another opportunity for Moriyasu to evaluate the team before facing the next competition. 
 Meanwhile, Brazil will meet host Singapore on the same date. 
 Both matches are part of the Mizuho Blue Challenge The Kallang Football Series Singapore 2026, which brings together Japan, Brazil, Paraguay, and Singapore. 
 For Japan, this series is a momentum to measure readiness to face teams from different regions. Collective play, effectiveness in finishing, and defensive consistency will be the focus. 
 Brazil has a similar task, especially in finding a balance between ball possession, attacking creativity, and the ability to face the opponent's quick transitions. 
 With the competition continuing to grow, the meeting between Japan and Brazil is now more than just a match between a traditional world football power and an Asian representative. 
 The duel also illustrates that Japan is increasingly capable of providing resistance to elite countries, while Brazil must continue to adapt to maintain its status as one of the main forces in international football.
